messages.content: The workshop was approved. Compare arriving Saturday evening with flying in Sunday morning. I want the real door-to-door risk and the full cost, including the extra hotel if I go Saturday.
I’ll compare both against the 12:30 p.m. Sunday check-in cutoff. Are the Hyatt conference dates still Sunday, August 18 through Wednesday, August 21, with the Wednesday 7:45 p.m. United return?
Yes. The Hyatt is only available those three nights, so Saturday would have to be somewhere nearby. I do not want to change hotels again after Sunday morning.

The strongest Saturday option is United nonstop from SFO at 1:15 p.m., arriving ORD at 7:22 p.m. A cancellable room at the Aloft Chicago Mag Mile is available Saturday for $238 including tax. It is about a five-minute taxi ride or a 12-minute walk from the Hyatt. You would check out Sunday, leave your bag with the Hyatt, and reach workshop check-in with several hours to spare.
What is the Sunday flight now? The 4:55 a.m. departure looked possible before, but I was concerned about the transfer from O’Hare.

United 4:55 a.m. nonstop is currently $486 round trip and arrives at 11:03 a.m. With an on-time arrival, a taxi could reach the Hyatt around 11:50 a.m.; the Blue Line plus the final walk is more likely to put you there around 12:10 p.m. That leaves only 20 to 40 minutes before check-in closes, with no useful margin for a delayed gate, checked bag, or traffic.
I will have only a carry-on. Price both plans from the same base, including the workshop, Hyatt, local transfer, and Saturday hotel where applicable.

Using the current rates: Sunday arrival is $486 airfare, $721 Hyatt total, $295 workshop fee, and about $58 for ORD taxis, for an estimated trip total of $1,560. Saturday arrival is $534 airfare, the same $721 Hyatt total, $295 workshop fee, $238 Aloft night, and about $76 across the airport and hotel-to-hotel transfers, for an estimated total of $1,864. Saturday costs about $304 more.
Why is that Sunday total lower than the $1,684 estimate from the approval summary?

The airfare has dropped by $96, and the earlier estimate carried a larger local-transport allowance. The Hyatt and workshop amounts are unchanged. I also rechecked the Hyatt total as three nights including taxes rather than using a rounded nightly estimate.
Check the practical issue with the split stay. Can the Aloft hold my bag Sunday morning, and can I reasonably get breakfast before moving to the Hyatt?

The Aloft lists luggage storage and Sunday breakfast service from 7:00 to 11:00 a.m., but breakfast is not included in the quoted rate. A workable sequence is breakfast around 8:00, checkout by 9:00, then taxi to the Hyatt. Even if the Hyatt room is not ready, its bell desk can hold luggage, leaving roughly three hours before workshop check-in closes. Luggage storage at both properties should still be confirmed directly because it is not guaranteed by the room rate.
The Sunday flight is too dependent on everything going exactly right. Use the Saturday plan. Give me the exact itinerary that is ready to book and flag anything that still needs confirmation.

Ready-for-booking itinerary: United nonstop SFO-ORD Saturday, August 17, 1:15-7:22 p.m.; Aloft Chicago Mag Mile for August 17-18 at $238 including tax on a cancellable rate; Hyatt conference hotel August 18-21 at $721 including tax; Sunday workshop at $295; and United nonstop ORD-SFO Wednesday, August 21 at 7:45 p.m. Estimated complete trip cost is $1,864, including about $76 for ground transport. Before purchase, confirm the Aloft cancellation deadline and Sunday luggage storage, confirm the Hyatt will hold luggage before room availability and link the Sunday-through-Wednesday stay to the conference reservation, and recheck that the workshop seat and $295 fee remain available with acceptable cancellation or substitution terms. No booking has been made.
